chapter: Zue Robertson, Bakke family and teachers
title: Teachers and lessons: Picou, Bechet and Barnes
summary: Barnes says he went to a well-known teacher and to Picou but did not keep up; he and Bechet went to teachers and learned in the district.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: No I couldn't answer on that. But I know that… That Shara Nees… Oh yeah. You see he was a teacher for most of the musicians. You see? Yeah I've heard a lot about him. Yeah. Now I don't know if he… he… he… he… teach those or not, but he was well known. All the musicians went to him, because I went to him myself. Yeah. Yeah. I went to him myself too. Oh you did. But I didn't keep up, but he tell me, oh that's pico too. I went to pico. Oh yeah, you did. Yeah I went to pico, but all the trouble, if you keep up you'll be a good boy, you don't want you silly, but I passed that up.
Did George Bakke help people? Did he ever give any regular lessons or help the young fellas?
Well George helped a whole lot of men. Yeah he helped…
I think he helped Sidney Bechet. Yeah. Sidney used to say he helped him, but…

Well Sidney, Sidney, Sidney, Sidney Bechet tell the truth about it. Me, him, and we used to go at Charles, then we'd go at pico. You see we used to go there, because why did we go there, then we used to go at the TU. But why did we go there, because we'd go in the district and pray in the place come tomorrow, I'll give you a list, you know.

And that's how come we had to go, but we used to know half of the town would go, and the next town would forget all about it. Well we didn't have music in our head, then we thought that was all nothing. Yeah, yeah. Because we could play, but we couldn't prove what we were doing. You know. That's a good one. How was Pico in the old days?
